concept.name: Rolling median
concept.definition: The rolling median is the median value of a series over a trailing window of fixed length that slides forward one observation at a time. It is a robust alternative to the rolling mean, insensitive to extreme values within the window.
concept.intuition: Instead of averaging the last N bars, take the middle one — a single spike can pull a mean around but cannot move the median much.
concept.mechanics: For window length w, sort the last w observations and take the middle value (average of the two middle values for even w) at each step. pandas supports rolling(window).median(), with the same right-edge labeling and min_periods conventions as other rolling aggregations.
concept.formula: RMed_t = median(x_{t−w+1}, …, x_t), where w is the window length.
concept.failure_modes: The median is a coarse, step-like statistic that can sit unchanged for many bars and then jump, which makes derivative-based signals awkward. It is also computationally heavier than the mean and still lagged by the window.
concept.misconceptions: Robustness to outliers is not always desirable — in return series, extreme moves are often the information, and median-filtering them away changes the risk picture.
concept.example: For the last 5 closes 100, 101, 99, 130, 102, the rolling median is 101 while the rolling mean is 106.4, showing the median's immunity to the 130 spike.
